extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants and practitioners (and patent examiners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required content/format rules for U.S. patent application specifications, abstracts, claims, sequence listings, and drawings, including examiner form paragraphs and corrective actions. Intended to ensure compliance with 37 CFR and MPEP rules during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A “Sequence Listing” is required on paper if the application discloses a nucleotide or amino acid sequence as defined in 37 CFR 1.821(a) and if the required “Sequence Listing” is not submitted as an electronic document either on compact disc or as a text file via the Office electronic filing system (EFS-Web).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2422.03 and 37 CFR 1.821-1.825. The requirement applies to all sequences disclosed in a given application, whether the sequences are claimed or not (MPEP § 2422.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of specification sections (design/plant/reissue)
rubrics_metrics.description: For arrangement of the sections of the specification in a design application see 37 CFR 1.154(b); for a plant application see 37 CFR 1.163(c); for a reissue application see 37 CFR 1.173(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use applicable form paragraphs (e.g., form paragraph 15.05 for a design application) and follow the cited CFR provisions for section arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of the Invention (Background)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should set forth the Background of the Invention in two parts. (1) Field of the Invention: A statement of the field of art to which the invention pertains; may include paraphrasing of applicable U.S. patent classification definitions. This item may also be titled 'Technical Field.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, concise statement identifying the technical field; avoid overly broad or vague language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Related Art (Background)
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) Description of the Related Art including information disclosed under 37 CFR 1.97 and 37 CFR 1.98: A description of the related art known to the applicant and, if applicable, references to specific related art and problems in the prior art which are solved by the applicant’s invention. May be titled 'Background Art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify known prior art and the problems addressed by the invention; preferably link the problems to advantages identified in the Summary of the Invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief Summary of the Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief summary or general statement of the invention as set forth in 37 CFR 1.73, separate and distinct from the abstract and directed toward the invention rather than the disclosure as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary may point out advantages or how it solves prior art problems; in chemical cases point out utility; set forth the nature/gist/inventive concept if possible; objects of the invention should be brief and only to the extent they aid understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief Description of the Several Views of the Drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to and brief description of the drawing(s) as set forth in 37 CFR 1.74.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide short, clear descriptions for each figure to assist reader understanding and cross-reference with detailed description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed Description of the Invention (preferred embodiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of the preferred embodiment(s) of the invention as required in 37 CFR 1.71. The description should be as short and specific as necessary to describe the invention adequately and accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit detailed description of conventional elements not necessary for understanding; where complicated or uncommon subject matter is involved, refer to another patent or readily available publication which adequately describes it. Avoid introducing new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: commencement and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims must commence on a separate sheet or electronic page (37 CFR 1.52(b)(3)). Where a claim sets forth a plurality of elements or steps, each element or step of the claim should be separated by a line indentation; plural indentations may segregate subcombinations or related steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 37 CFR 1.75 and MPEP § 608.01(i)-(p) for claim form; ensure claims start on separate page and use indentations consistently for clarity of claim structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract of the Disclosure: placement and length
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is a brief narrative of the disclosure as a whole, as concise as the disclosure permits, in a single paragraph preferably not exceeding 150 words, commencing on a separate sheet following the claims (37 CFR 1.72(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In national stage '371' applications an abstract published with the PCT may suffice; the IB abstract will be used by the USPTO. See MPEP § 1893.03(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract of the Disclosure: content (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent abstract is a concise statement of the technical disclosure and should include what is new in the art to which the invention pertains. The abstract should not refer to purported merits or speculative applications and should not compare the invention with the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If basic nature, abstract may cover entire disclosure; if improvement, include technical disclosure of the improvement; mention preferred modifications or alternatives by way of example. Generally limit to 50–150 words; narrative form; avoid legal phraseology and claim-style words like 'means' and 'said'. See MPEP § 608.01(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract of the Disclosure: chemical cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In chemical patent abstracts for compounds or compositions, give the general nature of the compound/composition and its use; exemplification of a species may illustrate the class. For processes, state the type of reaction, reagents and process conditions, generally illustrated by a single example unless variations are necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also other abstract form paragraphs (6.12–6.16). Keep chemical specifics concise and indicative of utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract of the Disclosure: language and form
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should be narrative, generally limited to a single paragraph on a separate sheet (preferably within 50–150 words). It should describe the disclosure sufficiently to assist readers in deciding whether to consult the full patent text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language should be clear and concise; do not repeat title information; avoid phrases that can be implied ('The disclosure concerns'); avoid legal phraseology and claim-like terms (e.g., 'means', 'said').

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of Invention must be descriptive
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention must be clearly indicative of the invention to which the claims are directed. If the title is not descriptive, a new title is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner suggests a change, use form paragraph 6.11.01 to propose suggested title (provide suggested title in bracket).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract missing or objected to
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application does not contain an abstract as required by 37 CFR 1.72(b), an abstract on a separate sheet is required. If the abstract is objected to (e.g., informalities, undue length, inclusion of legal phraseology), correction is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use certain form paragraphs during national stage prosecution if an abstract was published with the international application under PCT Article 21. For pro se applicants, follow up with additional form paragraphs (6.14–6.16) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of Claims (37 CFR 1.126)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original numbering of the claims must be preserved throughout prosecution. When claims are canceled, the remaining claims must not be renumbered. New claims must be numbered consecutively beginning with the next number after the highest numbered claims previously presented (whether entered or not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When indicating misnumbered and renumbered claims in form paragraphs, supply appropriate claim numbers and grammatical forms. See 37 CFR 1.126.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series of singular dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of singular dependent claims is permissible in which a dependent claim refers to a preceding claim which, in turn, refers to another preceding claim. A claim which depends from a dependent claim should not be separated by any claim which does not also depend from said dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep dependent claim sequence consistent; a dependent claim may refer to any preceding independent claim. Applicant’s sequence will generally not be changed. See MPEP § 608.01(n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of claims (separate sheet/electronic page)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must commence on a separate sheet or electronic page in accordance with 37 CFR 1.52(b)(3) and 1.75(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not, appropriate correction is required in response to the Office action (form paragraph 6.18.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of essential material is improper
rubrics_metrics.description: The incorporation of essential material in the specification by reference to an unpublished U.S. application, foreign application or patent, or to a publication is improper. Applicant must amend the disclosure to include the material if it is relied upon to overcome any objection, rejection, or other Office requirement (37 CFR 1.57(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment must be accompanied by a statement executed by the applicant or practitioner that the material being inserted is the material previously incorporated by reference and that the amendment contains no new matter. Make appropriate objections/rejections under 35 U.S.C. 132 and/or 35 U.S.C. 112 as necessary; follow with form paragraphs 7.31.01–7.31.04 where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineffective incorporation by reference — identify reason
rubrics_metrics.description: The attempt to incorporate subject matter by reference to [document] is ineffective because [reasons].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons may include omitted root words 'incorporate' or 'reference' (see 37 CFR 1.57(c)(1)) or insufficient identification of the reference document (37 CFR 1.57(c)(2)). Follow with corrective form paragraphs (e.g., 6.19.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of ineffective incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference will not be effective until correction is made to comply with 37 CFR 1.57(c), (d), or (e). If the incorporated material is relied upon to meet any outstanding requirement, correction must be made within any time period set by the Office for responding to the objection/rejection/requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction cannot be later than the close of prosecution as defined in 37 CFR 1.114(b) or abandonment. Any correction inserting material previously incorporated by reference must be accompanied by a statement that the material being inserted is the material previously incorporated and that the amendment contains no new matter (37 CFR 1.57(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade names and trademarks in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a trade name or mark used in commerce should be capitalized wherever it appears and be accompanied by generic terminology. Proprietary nature of marks should be respected to avoid adversely affecting their validity as commercial marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize each letter of the mark or include the proper symbol (™, SM, ®) where appropriate. Examiners may search TESS to determine registered marks. Use generic terminology alongside the mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected or new drawings required (competent draftsperson)
rubrics_metrics.description: New corrected drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required when drawings are noncompliant. Applicant is advised to employ a competent patent draftsperson outside the Office, as the USPTO does not prepare new drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrected drawings required in reply to an Office action to avoid abandonment; requirement will not be held in abeyance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings objected to: general replacement-sheet rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When drawings are objected to, corrected replacement drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required in reply. Any amended replacement sheet should include all figures appearing on the immediate prior version even if only one figure is amended; do not label an amended figure as 'amended'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a figure is canceled, remove it from the replacement sheet and renumber remaining figures and update the brief description of the drawings for consistency. Each drawing sheet submitted after filing must be labeled 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet'. Objections to drawings generally will not be held in abeyance. See MPEP § 608.02 and 37 CFR 1.121(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings objected to: details not shown (37 CFR 1.83(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings objected under 37 CFR 1.83(a) because they fail to show structural details described in the specification. Any structural detail essential for understanding should be shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrected drawing sheets required; include all prior-version figures on replacement sheets; may require marked-up copy annotated to show changes (form paragraph 6.27). Provide specifics in bracketed text identifying missing details. Objections will not be held in abeyance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings objected to: different numbers used for same part (1.84(p)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings objected because reference characters [1] and [2] have both been used to designate [3] (same part referenced by different numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit corrected drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d); identify the numbers and the part in brackets; include all figures on replacement sheets; objections will not be held in abeyance. May follow with form paragraph 6.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings objected to: same number used for different parts (1.84(p)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings objected because a single reference character [1] has been used to designate both [2] and [3] (same number for different parts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrected sheets required; identify the number and the differing parts in brackets; include prior-version figures on replacement sheets and avoid labeling 'amended'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings objected to: incomplete (37 CFR 1.83(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings objected to as incomplete under 37 CFR 1.83(b); when an invention is an improvement, drawings must exhibit the improved portion and enough of the old structure to show the connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply full explanation if incompleteness is not readily apparent; corrected replacement sheets required and objections will not be held in abeyance. May require marked-up copies showing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings objected to: modified forms of construction in same view (1.84(h)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings objected because a figure shows modified forms of construction in the same view (e.g., different embodiments shown together improperly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit corrected drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d); replacement sheets should follow standard replacement-sheet rules; do not label amended figures as 'amended'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings objected to: reference numbers mentioned in description but not in drawings (1.84(p)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings objected because they do not include reference sign(s) mentioned in the description; identify which reference characters are missing and where they first occur in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require corrected drawing sheets; alternatively, applicant may delete the reference characters from the description instead of adding them to drawings. May be followed by request for marked-up copy (form paragraph 6.27).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings objected to: reference numbers in drawings not mentioned in specification (1.84(p)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings objected because they include reference character(s) not mentioned in the description of the specification; correction requires either amended drawings or amendment to the specification to add the reference characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit corrected sheets or amend specification in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(b); include all prior-version figures on replacement sheets; specify characters and figure occurrences in bracketed text; may be followed by form paragraph 6.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter admits of illustration — draw under 37 CFR 1.81(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing to facilitate understanding, applicant is required to furnish a drawing under 37 CFR 1.81(c). No new matter may be introduced in the required drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date must be labeled 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' per 37 CFR 1.121(d). Use form paragraph 6.23.01 with PTOL-90 or PTO-90C when requiring drawings before examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter admits of illustration — time period for drawing (no examination of claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is given a TWO MONTH time period to submit a drawing in compliance with 37 CFR 1.81 when drawings are required and no examination of claims can be performed due to lack of illustration. Extensions available under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Failure to timely submit results in ABANDONMENT of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph sparingly and only where no examination can be performed due to lack of illustration. Use a PTOL-90 or PTO-90C form as a cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color photographs and color drawings — petition required
rubrics_metrics.description: Color photographs and color drawings are not accepted in utility applications unless a petition filed under 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2) is granted. The petition must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(h), one set of color drawings if via EFS-Web or three sets if not, and an amendment inserting specified language into the brief description of the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the prescribed first-paragraph language notifying the file contains color drawings and that copies with color drawings will be provided on request and payment. Color photographs accepted only if conditions for color drawings and black-and-white photographs are satisfied. Do not use in design applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings do not permit examination (poor quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are not of sufficient quality to permit examination; replacement drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required. Applicant is given a TWO MONTH time period to submit new drawings; failure will result in ABANDONMENT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement sheets should be labeled 'Replacement Sheet' and not obstruct drawing figures. Applicant must also provide a marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure including annotations indicating changes, labeled 'Annotated Sheet' and presented in the amendment or remarks section. Encourage submission before allowance to avoid term adjustment reductions (37 CFR 1.704(c)(10)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marked-up (annotated) copy requirement for amended drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: When corrected or replacement drawing figures are submitted, a marked-up (annotated) copy of the amended drawing figure(s) showing the changes must be provided and clearly labeled 'Annotated Sheet'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked-up copy must be presented in the amendment or remarks section explaining changes. See 37 CFR 1.121(d)(1)-(2). Failure to timely submit corrected drawings and marked-up copy will result in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idiomatic English requirement for substitute specification
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification in proper idiomatic English and in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b) is required when the specification as filed is not in idiomatic English. The substitute must be accompanied by a statement that it contains no new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may issue form paragraph 6.28 to require a substitute specification; ensure translations and edits do not introduce new matter; follow 37 CFR 1.52.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute specification required by examiner — identify reason
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification [1] the claims is required pursuant to 37 CFR 1.125(a) because [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the bracketed fields, identify the substitute specification's relation to claims and the specific reason(s) (e.g., language, format, new matter). Provide the required statement that the substitute contains no new matter.
